question: Explain the concept of time value of money. Distinguish between compounding and discounting, and explain the meaning of an annuity and a perpetuity.
sources: Time value of money (standard principle of financial mathematics)

points.label: Concept
points.description: A rupee received today is worth more than a rupee received in the future, because money today can be invested to earn interest.
points.basis: Time value of money: present money can earn a return

points.label: Reasons
points.description: Reasons include the opportunity to earn interest, inflation reducing purchasing power, the risk or uncertainty of future receipts, and the general preference for present consumption.
points.basis: Time value of money: reasons for preferring present money

points.label: Compounding and discounting
points.description: Compounding finds the future value of a present amount by adding interest on interest; discounting is the reverse and finds the present value of a future amount.
points.basis: Compound interest: future value and present value

points.label: Annuity
points.description: An annuity is a series of equal payments or receipts at equal intervals for a fixed period; in an ordinary annuity (annuity regular) payments are at the end of each period, in an annuity due at the beginning.
points.basis: Annuities: annuity regular and annuity due

points.label: Perpetuity
points.description: A perpetuity is an annuity that continues for ever; its present value is the periodic payment divided by the rate of interest per period.
points.basis: Perpetuity: present value equals payment divided by rate per period
